title: LFM2.5 Q4\_0 Checkpoints from Quantization-Aware Distillation
content:
Today, we release QAD Q4_0 GGUFs. These are updated 4-bit checkpoints for LFM2.5-230M, LFM2.5-350M, LFM2.5-1.2B-Instruct, and LFM2.5-2.6B. They allow developers to run LFM2.5 models at Q4_0 memory and speed without the usual quality drop:

Trained with Quantization-Aware Distillation (QAD): a high-precision teacher model is distilled into a quantized student model

Same memory and speed as native Q4_0: They keep the low memory footprint and high throughput of Q4_0 GGUFs

Recovery: 97% of their BF16 average accuracy lost to quantization is recovered

Benchmark results

For all four models, we compare their released GGUFs produced with post-training quantization (PTQ) against the trained QAD Q4_0 checkpoints on a benchmark suite spanning reasoning, instruction-following, tool use, and agentic capabilities: GPQA Diamond, MMLU-Pro, IFEval, IFBench, Multi-IF, and BFCLv4. The BF16 GGUF serves as the in-format ceiling. We also add one scale-appropriate math evaluation: GSM8K for LFM2.5-230M and LFM2.5-350M, and AIME25 for LFM2.5-1.2B-Instruct and LFM2.5-2.6B. We report the mean across five repeats.

Across all four models, QAD substantially improves the Q4_0 checkpoint. The QAD checkpoints retain 97.1%, 96.5%, 97.4%, and 96.6% of their respective BF16 baseline performance.

Speed and size on real edge hardware

We measure decode throughput for the four models LFM2.5-230M, LFM2.5-350M, LFM2.5-1.2B-Instruct, and LFM2.5-2.6B across four targets: MacBook Pro, NucBox EVO-X2, Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra, and Raspberry Pi 5. MacBook Pro and NucBox use GPU inference, while Samsung and Raspberry Pi use Arm CPU inference. BF16 and F16 are shown as full-precision references where profiled.

The 230M and 350M QAD Q4_0 checkpoints match Q5_K_M quality within evaluation variance at a 4-33% higher decode throughput. The 1.2B and 2.6B QAD Q4_0 checkpoints match Q4_K_M quality at a 3-14% higher throughput. The QAD Q4_0 checkpoints also match Unsloth's UD-Q4_K_XL (where applicable, for the 230M and 1.2B), a strong external post-training quantization checkpoint.

How to use QAD GGUFs

Use the files with llama.cpp or any runtime that supports GGUF Q4_0 artifacts.

llama-cli -hf LiquidAI/LFM2.5-350M \
  --hf-file LFM2.5-350M-QAD-Q4_0.gguf \
  -p "What is C. elegans?"

Get Started with QAD GGUFs

The QAD GGUFs are available on Hugging Face today: LFM2.5-230M, LFM2.5-350M, LFM2.5-1.2B-Instruct, and LFM2.5-2.6B.

We can't wait to see what you build.

Citation

For citations, please use the following reference or BibTeX:

Liquid AI, "LFM2.5 Q4_0: Quantization-Aware Distillation for Edge Deployment", Liquid AI Blog, Aug 2026.

Or use the BibTeX citation

  journal = {Liquid AI Blog},
  year = {2026},
  note = {www.liquid.ai/blog/qad},
}

translated_paragraphs: 今天，我们发布 QAD Q4_0 GGUF 格式模型。这些是针对 LFM2.5-230M、LFM2.5-350M、LFM2.5-1.2B-Instruct 和 LFM2.5-2.6B 的更新版 4-bit 检查点。它们使开发者能够在不牺牲质量的情况下，以 Q4_0 的内存占用和运行速度部署 LFM2.5 模型：
采用量化感知蒸馏（Quantization-Aware Distillation, QAD）训练：将高精度教师模型的知识蒸馏至量化学生模型中。
与原生 Q4_0 相同的内存占用和速度：保持 Q4_0 GGUF 的低内存占用和高吞吐量特性。
精度恢复：恢复了因量化而损失的 BF16 平均精度的 97%。
基准测试结果

针对上述四种模型，我们将通过后训练量化（PTQ）生成的已发布 GGUF 与经过 QAD 训练的 Q4_0 检查点在涵盖推理、指令遵循、工具使用和智能体能力的基准套件上进行对比评估，包括 GPQA Diamond、MMLU-Pro、IFEval、IFBench、Multi-IF 和 BFCLv4。其中，BF16 GGUF 作为同格式下的性能上限参考。此外，我们还增加了一项规模适配的数学能力评估：为 LFM2.5-230M 和 LFM2.5-350M 选用 GSM8K，为 LFM2.5-1.2B-Instruct 和 LFM2.5-2.6B 选用 AIME25。报告的结果为五次重复实验的平均值。
在所有四种模型上，QAD 显著提升了 Q4_0 检查点的性能。QAD 检查点分别保留了其各自 BF16 基线性能的 97.1%、96.5%、97.4% 和 96.6%。
在真实边缘硬件上的速度与尺寸表现

我们在四个目标设备上评估了 LFM2.5-230M、LFM2.5-350M、LFM2.5-1.2B-Instruct 和 LFM2.5-2.6B 这四个模型的解码吞吐量：MacBook Pro、NucBox EVO-X2、Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra 和 Raspberry Pi 5。MacBook Pro 和 NucBox 使用 GPU 推理，而 Samsung 和 Raspberry Pi 使用 Arm CPU 推理。在已进行性能剖析的情况下，BF16 和 F16 被作为全精度参考值展示。

230M 和 350M 的 QAD Q4_0 检查点在评估误差范围内达到了与 Q5_K_M 相当的质量，同时解码吞吐量提高了 4%-33%。1.2B 和 2.6B 的 QAD Q4_0 检查点达到了与 Q4_K_M 相当的质量，吞吐量提高了 3%-14%。QAD Q4_0 检查点还达到了 Unsloth 的 UD-Q4_K_XL（适用于 230M 和 1.2B 模型）的水平，这是一个强大的外部后训练量化检查点。
如何使用 QAD GGUF 文件
将文件用于 llama.cpp 或任何支持 GGUF Q4_0 格式的运行环境。

llama-cli -hf LiquidAI/LFM2.5-350M \
  --hf-file LFM2.5-350M-QAD-Q4_0.gguf \
  -p "什么是 C. elegans？"

title: How Much Memory Does Your Agent Actually Need?
content:
In our previous post, we compared ALTK-Evolve with ACE and showed that how you deliver an agent's self-distilled guidelines — a few retrieved per task vs. the whole set injected — drives both accuracy and cost. This post steps back to the question that comes before it: how much should you give it?

Equipping an agent with agentic memory sounds simple: distill lessons from its past work, put them back in context, and more experience should mean better performance. It doesn't always work that way. When we scaled the evaluation to eight models — from a 30B dense model to frontier proprietary systems — one finding stood out:

Agentic memory is not a feature you switch on. It's a dose you calibrate to the model.

TL;DR

ALTK-Evolve lets an agent learn from its own past trajectories: distilling reusable guidelines and injecting them back at inference time, with no weight updates and no human annotation.

The right dose differs by model tier: strong models with headroom want the full guideline set, weaker models do best with a compact core plus per-task retrieval, and saturated models show no measurable gain.

Curated retrieval can be both the most accurate and the cheapest option: gpt-oss-120b gained +16.1pp task completion at only +5% tokens — and prompt caching keeps even the full guideline set affordable in production.

The Key Insight: Dosage Depends on Capability

Not every model benefits from the same amount of memory. Across eight models spanning the capability spectrum, we saw three recurring patterns:

Strong models with headroom want the full guideline set — every guideline, including rare edge-case lessons. They have the capacity to absorb and apply all of it. DeepSeek-V3.2 (671B MoE) climbed +9.5 percentage points in task completion when given its full self-mined guideline set.

Smaller or weaker models get drowned by a large guideline set. For these, a tight, high-confidence core plus a handful of task-relevant guidelines retrieved per task works best. gpt-oss-120b (117B MoE) gained +16.1pp with this selective approach — while the full guideline set gained less and cost ~50% more tokens.

Already-saturated models show no measurable gain. We call this the saturated pattern — the label describes what we observed, not a proven cause. The model may already have been near its ceiling on these tasks, the guidelines may not have addressed its remaining failures, or it may not have applied the guidance effectively. GLM-5 (745B MoE) sat here in our runs.

What puts a model into one pattern rather than another isn't simply parameter count. Benchmark headroom, context-window size, architecture, guideline quality, and task distribution all appear to shape where a model lands, and separating those factors is ongoing work. The practical takeaway holds either way: the right dose of memory depends on the model, and we can calibrate it.

Learning happens around the model, not inside it

"Memory" here doesn't mean replaying a past transcript. It means a guideline set — strategies that worked, mistakes to avoid, and edge cases — distilled from the agent's own prior trajectories. The loop is straightforward:

The agent attempts tasks and produces trajectories.

ALTK-Evolve extracts behavioral guidelines from both its successful and unsuccessful runs.

It consolidates those guidelines into a reusable set.

At inference time, the agent receives either the full guideline set or a task-relevant selection of it.

No model weights are updated. The learning loop changes the guidance available to the agent, not the underlying model — which is exactly why it's cheap to adopt and portable across the eight models we tested.

Results Across the Spectrum

We evaluated on AppWorld — 585 multi-step tasks (168 test_normal + 417 test_challenge) across 9 simulated apps (calendars, messaging, payments, and so on). Tasks are scored two ways: whether the agent fully completes each task (TGC — Task Goal Completion) and whether every variant of a scenario passes (SGC — Scenario Goal Completion, a stricter, all-or-nothing bar). Full definitions are in the appendix.

The three configurations we compare

Equipping an agent with agentic memory sounds simple: distill lessons from its past work, put them back in context, and more experience should mean better performance. It doesn't always work that way. When we scaled the evaluation to eight models — from a 30B dense model to frontier proprietary systems — one finding stood out:

Agentic memory is not a feature you switch on. It's a dose you calibrate to the model.

Strong models with headroom want the full guideline set — every guideline, including rare edge-case lessons. They have the capacity to absorb and apply all of it. DeepSeek-V3.2 (671B MoE) climbed +9.5 percentage points in task completion when given its full self-mined guideline set.

original_paragraphs: In our previous post, we compared ALTK-Evolve with ACE and showed that how you deliver an agent's self-distilled guidelines — a few retrieved per task vs. the whole set injected — drives both accuracy and cost. This post steps back to the question that comes before it: how much should you give it?

Equipping an agent with agentic memory sounds simple: distill lessons from its past work, put them back in context, and more experience should mean better performance. It doesn't always work that way. When we scaled the evaluation to eight models — from a 30B dense model to frontier proprietary systems — one finding stood out:
Agentic memory is not a feature you switch on. It's a dose you calibrate to the model.
TL;DR
ALTK-Evolve lets an agent learn from its own past trajectories: distilling reusable guidelines and injecting them back at inference time, with no weight updates and no human annotation.

The right dose differs by model tier: strong models with headroom want the full guideline set, weaker models do best with a compact core plus per-task retrieval, and saturated models show no measurable gain.

Curated retrieval can be both the most accurate and the cheapest option: gpt-oss-120b gained +16.1pp task completion at only +5% tokens — and prompt caching keeps even the full guideline set affordable in production.
The Key Insight: Dosage Depends on Capability
Not every model benefits from the same amount of memory. Across eight models spanning the capability spectrum, we saw three recurring patterns:

Strong models with headroom want the full guideline set — every guideline, including rare edge-case lessons. They have the capacity to absorb and apply all of it. DeepSeek-V3.2 (671B MoE) climbed +9.5 percentage points in task completion when given its full self-mined guideline set.

Smaller or weaker models get drowned by a large guideline set. For these, a tight, high-confidence core plus a handful of task-relevant guidelines retrieved per task works best. gpt-oss-120b (117B MoE) gained +16.1pp with this selective approach — while the full guideline set gained less and cost ~50% more tokens.

Already-saturated models show no measurable gain. We call this the saturated pattern — the label describes what we observed, not a proven cause. The model may already have been near its ceiling on these tasks, the guidelines may not have addressed its remaining failures, or it may not have applied the guidance effectively. GLM-5 (745B MoE) sat here in our runs.

What puts a model into one pattern rather than another isn't simply parameter count. Benchmark headroom, context-window size, architecture, guideline quality, and task distribution all appear to shape where a model lands, and separating those factors is ongoing work. The practical takeaway holds either way: the right dose of memory depends on the model, and we can calibrate it.
Learning happens around the model, not inside it

"Memory" here doesn't mean replaying a past transcript. It means a guideline set — strategies that worked, mistakes to avoid, and edge cases — distilled from the agent's own prior trajectories. The loop is straightforward:
The agent attempts tasks and produces trajectories.
ALTK-Evolve extracts behavioral guidelines from both its successful and unsuccessful runs.
It consolidates those guidelines into a reusable set.
At inference time, the agent receives either the full guideline set or a task-relevant selection of it.

No model weights are updated. The learning loop changes the guidance available to the agent, not the underlying model — which is exactly why it's cheap to adopt and portable across the eight models we tested.
Results Across the Spectrum

We evaluated on AppWorld — 585 multi-step tasks (168 test_normal + 417 test_challenge) across 9 simulated apps (calendars, messaging, payments, and so on). Tasks are scored two ways: whether the agent fully completes each task (TGC — Task Goal Completion) and whether every variant of a scenario passes (SGC — Scenario Goal Completion, a stricter, all-or-nothing bar). Full definitions are in the appendix.
The three configurations we compare
Because the confusing part of any memory study is what's actually in the context window, we define the configurations up front.

Both memory configurations draw from the same guideline set, mined once (via the loop above) from AppWorld's training split only. What changes between them is only how that one set is delivered — the full guideline set injects all of it every step, while curated retrieval delivers a selected subset — never how the guidelines were produced, and no test-split data ever goes into building it.
Configuration
What's in the agent's context
Baseline
No memory — the agent as shipped.
Full guideline set
Every mined guideline, injected on every ReAct step.
Curated retrieval
A fixed, high-confidence core of those same guidelines plus a few task-relevant ones retrieved for each task (a fixed portion + a variable portion).

The number of guidelines a model mines depends on its own capability, so we report configurations by strategy — "full guideline set" vs. "curated retrieval" — rather than by raw counts, which aren't comparable across models.

Reading the SGC column, the stricter metric usually moves more than TGC — DeepSeek's SGC jumps +16.1pp against a +9.5pp TGC gain — because good guidelines especially help an agent clear every variant of a scenario, not just the average case. And the effect doesn't disappear at the top of the range: GPT-5.5 and Opus, both near the ceiling on TGC, still gain +7.2 and +7.1pp SGC respectively. Memory keeps paying off as long as a model has a remaining failure mode to target.
The Cheapest Memory Strategy Can Also Be the Best
A practical concern: injecting a full guideline set inflates every ReAct step's input, because the guidelines are re-sent each turn. Here's what we observed:

Two takeaways:

Curated retrieval keeps cost near baseline. For weaker models, where selection wins on accuracy, it also wins on cost — the best of both worlds (+16.1pp TGC at only +5% tokens for gpt-oss-120b). Better performance here does not require more inference cost.

Memory doesn't blow up the reasoning loop. DeepSeek runs about the same number of ReAct steps with memory as without (≈18–19 on average), so the added cost is input-token inflation, not longer trajectories.

The real efficiency lever in production is prompt caching: the static portion of the guideline set is identical across steps and can be cached, cutting effective cost substantially. Cache-aware prompt design — keeping the shared guideline-set prefix stable so it stays cacheable — is worth engineering for. We also hypothesize that context-window size plays a role: models with larger windows may absorb the full guideline set more effectively, while smaller-context models benefit more from retrieval that keeps injected content compact. We have not yet run controlled experiments isolating this factor.
Memory Should Be Calibrated, Not Merely Accumulated
The lesson isn't to give an agent everything it has learned. It's to give it the amount of experience it can actually use.
For weak models, that means a compact core plus a few task-specific lessons — which, conveniently, is also the cheapest option.
For strong models with headroom, it means preserving the full guideline set, kept affordable in production via prompt caching.
For saturated models, it means spending no extra context until their remaining failure modes are better understood.
The gains are real across the board — automatic, leakage-free, and requiring no human annotation — but only when the dose fits the model.
What's Next
This is a starting point, not the finish line:

A learned selector. Our current retrieval ranks guidelines by cosine similarity, which we've shown doesn't perfectly predict which guidelines help a given task. A selector trained on outcome signal is the natural next step.
Memory for very weak models. Below a minimum capability baseline, self-distillation lacks signal. Teacher-distilled memory for very weak models is a separate problem we're exploring.
Beyond AppWorld. These results are validated on AppWorld — a rigorous multi-step benchmark, but a single one. Broader agent benchmarks and real-world deployments are in progress.
Isolating context window. As above, we want controlled experiments that separate context-window size from raw capability.
Try the ALTK-Evolve library — which includes the extraction, consolidation, and retrieval pipeline used here — or read the full technical report for the complete method and ablations.
Appendix: Understanding the Metrics
AppWorld tasks are graded by two metrics, both reported as percentages (higher is better):
TGC — Task Goal Completion. The share of individual tasks the agent completes fully and correctly. This is the headline "did it get the job done" number.

SGC — Scenario Goal Completion. A stricter, all-or-nothing metric. Each scenario bundles several variants of the same task (the same request with different data, phrasing, or edge conditions). SGC counts a scenario as passing only if the agent succeeds on every variant. It measures reliability — an agent that solves a task most of the time but fails on one variant scores on TGC but not on SGC.
translated_paragraphs: 在上一篇博文中，我们将 ALTK-Evolve 与 ACE 进行了比较，并展示了如何交付智能体的自蒸馏指南——是针对每个任务检索少量指南，还是将全部指南注入上下文——这一方式会同时影响准确性和成本。本篇博客则退一步，探讨在此之前的问题：你应该给予它多少量？
为智能体配备“代理式记忆”听起来很简单：从其过往工作中提炼经验教训，将其重新放入上下文之中，那么经验越多，性能应该越好。但事实并非总是如此。当我们将评估扩展至八种模型——从 30B 参数的稠密模型到前沿的专有系统——时，一个发现尤为突出：
代理式记忆不是一个可以简单开启的功能，而是一种需要根据模型进行校准的剂量。
TL;DR（太长不看版）
ALTK-Evolve 让智能体能够从自身过去的轨迹中学习：提炼可复用的指南，并在推理阶段将其注入，无需更新权重，也无需人工标注。
合适的剂量因模型层级而异：能力较强、尚有提升空间的模型适合使用完整的指南集；较弱的模型则在采用精简核心指南加上按任务检索时表现最佳；而已经饱和的模型则未显示出任何可测量的收益。
精心策划的检索既可以是准确率最高的选项，也可以是最具成本效益的方案：gpt-oss-120b 仅增加 5% 的 token 消耗，便使任务完成率提升了 16.1 个百分点；而提示缓存技术甚至能让生产环境中使用完整的指南集也变得经济实惠。
关键洞察：剂量取决于模型能力
并非所有模型都能从相同数量的记忆中受益。在跨越整个能力谱系的八种模型中，我们观察到三种反复出现的模式：
具有提升空间的强大模型需要完整的指南集——包括所有指南，乃至罕见边缘案例的经验教训。它们具备吸收并应用全部内容的容量。在获得其完整自挖掘指南集后，DeepSeek-V3.2（671B MoE）的任务完成率提升了9.5个百分点。
较小或较弱的模型会被庞大的指南集淹没。对于这些模型而言，采用一个紧密且高置信度的核心指南集，并在每次任务中检索少量与任务相关的指南效果最佳。gpt-oss-120b（117B MoE）通过这种选择性方法获得了16.1个百分点的提升；相比之下，使用完整指南集带来的增益较少，且消耗了约50%更多的token。
已经饱和的模型未显示出可测量的提升。我们将此称为“饱和模式”——该标签仅描述我们所观察到的现象，而非已证实的原因。这些模型在这些任务上可能已接近性能上限，指南可能未能解决其剩余的错误，或者它未能有效地应用指导。在我们的实验中，GLM-5（745B MoE）就处于这一状态。
决定模型落入哪种模式的因素并非仅仅是参数量。基准测试中的提升空间、上下文窗口大小、架构、指南质量以及任务分布等因素似乎共同决定了模型的定位，而分离这些因素仍是正在进行的工作。无论属于哪种模式，实际的启示都是一致的：所需的记忆剂量取决于具体模型，我们可以对其进行校准。
学习发生在模型周围，而非模型内部。
此处的“记忆”并非指回放过去的操作记录，而是指一套从智能体自身先前轨迹中提炼出的行为准则——包括行之有效的策略、需避免的错误以及边缘情况。其循环过程十分直接：
智能体尝试执行任务并生成相应的操作轨迹。
ALTK-Evolve 从其成功和失败的运行中提取行为准则。
随后将这些准则整合为可复用的集合。
在推理阶段，智能体会接收完整的准则集，或仅接收与当前任务相关的部分准则。
该过程不更新模型权重。学习循环改变的是智能体可用的指导信息，而非底层模型本身——这正是其采用成本低且能移植到我们测试的八种模型中的原因。
全谱系评估结果
我们在 AppWorld 上进行了评估，涵盖 585 个多步任务（168 个 test_normal + 417 个 test_challenge），涉及 9 款模拟应用（如日历、即时通讯、支付等）。任务评分采用两种方式：一是智能体是否完全完成每个任务（TGC，即任务目标完成率）；二是场景的所有变体是否均通过（SGC，即场景目标完成率，这是一种更严格的“全有或全无”标准）。完整定义见附录。
我们比较的三种配置
由于任何记忆研究中最令人困惑的部分在于上下文窗口中实际包含的内容，因此我们预先明确定义了这些配置。
两种记忆配置均源自同一套指南集，该指南集仅从 AppWorld 的训练集中通过上述循环提取一次。它们之间的唯一区别在于这套指南集的交付方式——完整指南集会在每一步骤中注入全部内容，而精选检索则仅提供每个任务所需的选定子集（包含固定部分和可变部分）。指南的生产方式从未改变，且测试集数据也从未用于构建该指南集。
配置
智能体上下文中的内容
基线
无记忆——即原始发布的智能体。
完整指南集
每次 ReAct 步骤都注入所有已挖掘的指南。
精选检索
这些相同指南中固定、高置信度的核心部分，加上为每个任务检索出的少量相关任务指南（由固定部分和可变部分组成）。
模型挖掘的指南数量取决于其自身能力，因此我们按策略（“完整指南集”与“精选检索”）而非原始数量来报告配置，因为不同模型间的原始数量不可直接比较。
三种模式一览
在八款模型扫描中，以测试集正常情况下的任务完成率（TGC）衡量的代表性模型：

记忆不会导致推理循环爆炸。DeepSeek 在启用记忆与未启用记忆时，运行的 ReAct 步骤数大致相同（平均约 18–19 步），因此增加的成本主要来自输入 token 的膨胀，而非更长的轨迹。
在生产环境中真正的效率杠杆是提示缓存：指南集的部分静态内容在各步骤间保持一致，可以被缓存，从而大幅降低有效成本。值得投入工程资源进行“感知缓存”的提示设计——保持共享指南集前缀的稳定，以确保其可被缓存。我们还假设上下文窗口大小会发挥作用：拥有更大窗口的模型可能更有效地吸收完整的指南集，而上下文较小的模型则更受益于通过检索来保持注入内容的紧凑性。我们尚未运行隔离该因素的受控实验。
记忆应当经过校准，而非仅仅不断累积
这一教训并非要把智能体所学的一切全部给它，而是只给它真正能够利用的经验量。
对于较弱的模型，这意味着一个精简的核心加上几条特定任务的经验——这恰好也是最经济的方案。
对于有余力的强模型，这意味着保留完整的指南集，并通过生产环境中的提示缓存来维持其成本效益。
对于已饱和的模型，这意味着在其剩余故障模式得到更好理解之前，不再消耗额外的上下文空间。
这些收益普遍存在——自动化、无信息泄露，且无需人工标注——但前提是剂量必须与模型相匹配。
下一步是什么
这是一个起点，而非终点：
智能选择器。我们当前的检索方法基于余弦相似度对指南进行排序，但我们已证明这种方法并不能完美预测哪些指南对特定任务有帮助。训练一个以结果信号为目标的智能选择器是自然且必要的下一步。
针对极弱模型的记忆机制。当模型能力低于最低基线时，自蒸馏缺乏有效的学习信号。针对极弱模型的教师蒸馏记忆是一个我们正在探索的独立问题。
超越 AppWorld。这些结果在 AppWorld——一个严格的单步多步骤基准测试中得到了验证，但它仅是单一基准。更广泛的智能体基准测试和真实世界部署工作正在进行中。
隔离上下文窗口。如上所述，我们需要受控实验来区分上下文窗口大小与原始模型能力的影响。
尝试使用 ALTK-Evolve 库——其中包含此处使用的提取、整合和检索管道——或阅读完整的技术报告，了解详细的方法和消融实验结果。
附录：理解评估指标
AppWorld 任务通过两项指标进行评估，均以百分比表示（数值越高越好）：
TGC——任务目标完成率（Task Goal Completion）。指智能体完全且正确完成的单个任务所占比例。这是衡量“是否成功完成任务”的核心指标。
SGC——场景目标完成率（Scenario Goal Completion）。这是一种更严格的全有或全无型指标。每个场景包含同一任务的多个变体（即相同请求但数据、措辞或边界条件不同）。只有当智能体在所有变体上均取得成功时，该场景才算通过。SGC 衡量的是可靠性——如果一个智能体在大多数情况下能完成任务，但在某个变体上失败，它会在 TGC 中获得分数，但在 SGC 中则不会得分。

translated_blocks.text: 在上一篇博文中，我们将 ALTK-Evolve 与 ACE 进行了比较，并展示了如何交付智能体的自蒸馏指南——是针对每个任务检索少量指南，还是将全部指南注入上下文——这一方式会同时影响准确性和成本。本篇博客则退一步，探讨在此之前的问题：你应该给予它多少量？
为智能体配备“代理式记忆”听起来很简单：从其过往工作中提炼经验教训，将其重新放入上下文之中，那么经验越多，性能应该越好。但事实并非总是如此。当我们将评估扩展至八种模型——从 30B 参数的稠密模型到前沿的专有系统——时，一个发现尤为突出：

children.text: 代理式记忆不是一个可以简单开启的功能，而是一种需要根据模型进行校准的剂量。

translated_blocks.text: TL;DR（太长不看版）

items.text: ALTK-Evolve 让智能体能够从自身过去的轨迹中学习：提炼可复用的指南，并在推理阶段将其注入，无需更新权重，也无需人工标注。
合适的剂量因模型层级而异：能力较强、尚有提升空间的模型适合使用完整的指南集；较弱的模型则在采用精简核心指南加上按任务检索时表现最佳；而已经饱和的模型则未显示出任何可测量的收益。
精心策划的检索既可以是准确率最高的选项，也可以是最具成本效益的方案：gpt-oss-120b 仅增加 5% 的 token 消耗，便使任务完成率提升了 16.1 个百分点；而提示缓存技术甚至能让生产环境中使用完整的指南集也变得经济实惠。

translated_blocks.text: 关键洞察：剂量取决于模型能力
并非所有模型都能从相同数量的记忆中受益。在跨越整个能力谱系的八种模型中，我们观察到三种反复出现的模式：

items.text: 具有提升空间的强大模型需要完整的指南集——包括所有指南，乃至罕见边缘案例的经验教训。它们具备吸收并应用全部内容的容量。在获得其完整自挖掘指南集后，DeepSeek-V3.2（671B MoE）的任务完成率提升了9.5个百分点。
较小或较弱的模型会被庞大的指南集淹没。对于这些模型而言，采用一个紧密且高置信度的核心指南集，并在每次任务中检索少量与任务相关的指南效果最佳。gpt-oss-120b（117B MoE）通过这种选择性方法获得了16.1个百分点的提升；相比之下，使用完整指南集带来的增益较少，且消耗了约50%更多的token。
已经饱和的模型未显示出可测量的提升。我们将此称为“饱和模式”——该标签仅描述我们所观察到的现象，而非已证实的原因。这些模型在这些任务上可能已接近性能上限，指南可能未能解决其剩余的错误，或者它未能有效地应用指导。在我们的实验中，GLM-5（745B MoE）就处于这一状态。

translated_blocks.text: 决定模型落入哪种模式的因素并非仅仅是参数量。基准测试中的提升空间、上下文窗口大小、架构、指南质量以及任务分布等因素似乎共同决定了模型的定位，而分离这些因素仍是正在进行的工作。无论属于哪种模式，实际的启示都是一致的：所需的记忆剂量取决于具体模型，我们可以对其进行校准。
学习发生在模型周围，而非模型内部。
此处的“记忆”并非指回放过去的操作记录，而是指一套从智能体自身先前轨迹中提炼出的行为准则——包括行之有效的策略、需避免的错误以及边缘情况。其循环过程十分直接：

items.text: 智能体尝试执行任务并生成相应的操作轨迹。
ALTK-Evolve 从其成功和失败的运行中提取行为准则。
随后将这些准则整合为可复用的集合。
在推理阶段，智能体会接收完整的准则集，或仅接收与当前任务相关的部分准则。

translated_blocks.text: 该过程不更新模型权重。学习循环改变的是智能体可用的指导信息，而非底层模型本身——这正是其采用成本低且能移植到我们测试的八种模型中的原因。
全谱系评估结果
我们在 AppWorld 上进行了评估，涵盖 585 个多步任务（168 个 test_normal + 417 个 test_challenge），涉及 9 款模拟应用（如日历、即时通讯、支付等）。任务评分采用两种方式：一是智能体是否完全完成每个任务（TGC，即任务目标完成率）；二是场景的所有变体是否均通过（SGC，即场景目标完成率，这是一种更严格的“全有或全无”标准）。完整定义见附录。
我们比较的三种配置
由于任何记忆研究中最令人困惑的部分在于上下文窗口中实际包含的内容，因此我们预先明确定义了这些配置。
两种记忆配置均源自同一套指南集，该指南集仅从 AppWorld 的训练集中通过上述循环提取一次。它们之间的唯一区别在于这套指南集的交付方式——完整指南集会在每一步骤中注入全部内容，而精选检索则仅提供每个任务所需的选定子集（包含固定部分和可变部分）。指南的生产方式从未改变，且测试集数据也从未用于构建该指南集。

headers.text: 智能体上下文中的内容

rows.text: 无记忆——即原始发布的智能体。
每次 ReAct 步骤都注入所有已挖掘的指南。
这些相同指南中固定、高置信度的核心部分，加上为每个任务检索出的少量相关任务指南（由固定部分和可变部分组成）。

translated_blocks.text: 模型挖掘的指南数量取决于其自身能力，因此我们按策略（“完整指南集”与“精选检索”）而非原始数量来报告配置，因为不同模型间的原始数量不可直接比较。
三种模式一览
在八款模型扫描中，以测试集正常情况下的任务完成率（TGC）衡量的代表性模型：
图1. 三种观察到的模式中的代表性模型。柱状图显示基线与最佳记忆配置在 AppWorld 测试集正常情况下的 TGC；x轴从40%开始以便更清晰地展示差异。仅看 TGC 会低估更大的 SGC 提升——详见下方表格中的 SGC 列。
该图绘制的是 TGC 以保持可读性；下表补充了更严格的 SGC 指标，其中增益往往更大：

rows.text: 表现强劲，仍有提升空间
表现强劲，仍有提升空间

translated_blocks.text: 记忆不会导致推理循环爆炸。DeepSeek 在启用记忆与未启用记忆时，运行的 ReAct 步骤数大致相同（平均约 18–19 步），因此增加的成本主要来自输入 token 的膨胀，而非更长的轨迹。
在生产环境中真正的效率杠杆是提示缓存：指南集的部分静态内容在各步骤间保持一致，可以被缓存，从而大幅降低有效成本。值得投入工程资源进行“感知缓存”的提示设计——保持共享指南集前缀的稳定，以确保其可被缓存。我们还假设上下文窗口大小会发挥作用：拥有更大窗口的模型可能更有效地吸收完整的指南集，而上下文较小的模型则更受益于通过检索来保持注入内容的紧凑性。我们尚未运行隔离该因素的受控实验。
记忆应当经过校准，而非仅仅不断累积

headers.text: 这一教训并非要把智能体所学的一切全部给它，而是只给它真正能够利用的经验量。
对于较弱的模型，这意味着一个精简的核心加上几条特定任务的经验——这恰好也是最经济的方案。
对于有余力的强模型，这意味着保留完整的指南集，并通过生产环境中的提示缓存来维持其成本效益。
对于已饱和的模型，这意味着在其剩余故障模式得到更好理解之前，不再消耗额外的上下文空间。
这些收益普遍存在——自动化、无信息泄露，且无需人工标注——但前提是剂量必须与模型相匹配。

rows.text: 这是一个起点，而非终点：
智能选择器。我们当前的检索方法基于余弦相似度对指南进行排序，但我们已证明这种方法并不能完美预测哪些指南对特定任务有帮助。训练一个以结果信号为目标的智能选择器是自然且必要的下一步。
针对极弱模型的记忆机制。当模型能力低于最低基线时，自蒸馏缺乏有效的学习信号。针对极弱模型的教师蒸馏记忆是一个我们正在探索的独立问题。
超越 AppWorld。这些结果在 AppWorld——一个严格的单步多步骤基准测试中得到了验证，但它仅是单一基准。更广泛的智能体基准测试和真实世界部署工作正在进行中。
隔离上下文窗口。如上所述，我们需要受控实验来区分上下文窗口大小与原始模型能力的影响。
尝试使用 ALTK-Evolve 库——其中包含此处使用的提取、整合和检索管道——或阅读完整的技术报告，了解详细的方法和消融实验结果。
AppWorld 任务通过两项指标进行评估，均以百分比表示（数值越高越好）：
TGC——任务目标完成率（Task Goal Completion）。指智能体完全且正确完成的单个任务所占比例。这是衡量“是否成功完成任务”的核心指标。
SGC——场景目标完成率（Scenario Goal Completion）。这是一种更严格的全有或全无型指标。每个场景包含同一任务的多个变体（即相同请求但数据、措辞或边界条件不同）。只有当智能体在所有变体上均取得成功时，该场景才算通过。SGC 衡量的是可靠性——如果一个智能体在大多数情况下能完成任务，但在某个变体上失败，它会在 TGC 中获得分数，但在 SGC 中则不会得分。

title: Get closer to the game with Gemini and Pixel
content:
Google is partnering with five iconic football clubs—Arsenal, FC Barcelona, FC Bayern München, Liverpool, and Paris Saint-Germain—to bring fans closer to the action. You can now use Gemini for deep match insights and Pixel cameras for exclusive, behind-the-scenes content that highlights both men’s and women’s teams. Follow the official club and Google social media channels to see this new content and access exclusive team wallpapers.

Google’s "Get closer to the game with Gemini and Pixel" highlights new football partnerships.

Gemini provides fans with deep match insights, stats, and instant answers during games.

Pixel cameras will capture exclusive, behind-the-scenes content for fans to enjoy.

These partnerships aim to boost global visibility for women’s football teams.

You can now access official club wallpapers to customize your Pixel device.

Google is partnering with five famous football clubs to bring fans closer to the action. You can use Gemini to get quick stats and insights about your favorite teams. They’re also using Pixel cameras to share cool, behind-the-scenes content from both men’s and women’s matches. This partnership aims to give women’s football the extra attention it deserves.

Explore other styles:

General summary

Bullet points

Basic explainer

We’re launching new long-term partnerships with five of the world’s most iconic football clubs: Arsenal FC, FC Barcelona, FC Bayern München, Liverpool FC, and Paris Saint-Germain. As their Official Consumer AI and Official Smartphone Partner, Gemini and Pixel are coming together to help put fans right at the heart of the action.Supercharging match days with GeminiFootball culture is fueled by the stories that define the game, both on and off the pitch. With Gemini as their personal assistant, supporters can dive deeper into match and club insights and stay connected to the moments that matter most.Whether you’re dissecting a mid-game formation change in the midst of a European club clash or settling a post-match debate with precise head-to-head history, Gemini’s advanced agentic capabilities proactively handle tasks on your behalf and put answers right in your hands, keeping you at the heart of the action.Bringing you a new angle on the game with PixelAs the Official Smartphone Partner, Google Pixel is working with club media teams to capture all the raw, unfiltered moments and emotions behind the scenes of the match.Through our signature "Shot on Pixel" series, club social teams will use Pixel’s camera with our AI tools to share fresh, authentic perspectives. Plus, you can already show your colors by customizing your Pixel 11 device with official club wallpapers.Raising the visibility of women's footballA fundamental part of these partnerships is our commitment to help closing the visibility gap in women’s football. Record-breaking crowds are watching women's tournaments, yet the game still lacks the media coverage and visibility it deserves.By partnering equally across both men’s and women’s teams, we are putting our technology to work to help change that. Together with the clubs we will capture jaw dropping pitch-side action, produce unforgettable content, and amplify the reach of the women’s game globally - driving the visibility needed to help inspire the next generation of players and fans.Across our partner clubsWe are incredibly proud to collaborate with Arsenal FC, FC Barcelona, FC Bayern München, Liverpool FC and Paris Saint-Germain - clubs that represent the very best of football heritage and community across Europe's top leagues. Together, we will deliver exclusive behind-the-scenes content, matchday insights and new AI-powered fan experiences to bring supporters closer to the stories and stats that define their favorite teams. Follow our partner clubs' official channels — Arsenal FC, FC Barcelona, FC Bayern München, Liverpool FC and Paris Saint-Germain and @GooglePixel and @GoogleGemini — to see these stories unfold and get closer to the game this season. Get the latest news from Google in your inbox Sign up for our newsletters with product updates, event information, special offers, and more. Done. Just one step more. Check your inbox to confirm your subscription. You can also subscribe with a different email address. Your information will be used in accordance with Google's privacy policy. You may opt out at any time. POSTED IN:

We’re launching new long-term partnerships with five of the world’s most iconic football clubs: Arsenal FC, FC Barcelona, FC Bayern München, Liverpool FC, and Paris Saint-Germain. As their Official Consumer AI and Official Smartphone Partner, Gemini and Pixel are coming together to help put fans right at the heart of the action.Supercharging match days with GeminiFootball culture is fueled by the stories that define the game, both on and off the pitch. With Gemini as their personal assistant, supporters can dive deeper into match and club insights and stay connected to the moments that matter most.Whether you’re dissecting a mid-game formation change in the midst of a European club clash or settling a post-match debate with precise head-to-head history, Gemini’s advanced agentic capabilities proactively handle tasks on your behalf and put answers right in your hands, keeping you at the heart of the action.Bringing you a new angle on the game with PixelAs the Official Smartphone Partner, Google Pixel is working with club media teams to capture all the raw, unfiltered moments and emotions behind the scenes of the match.Through our signature "Shot on Pixel" series, club social teams will use Pixel’s camera with our AI tools to share fresh, authentic perspectives. Together with the clubs we will capture jaw dropping pitch-side action, produce unforgettable content, and amplify the reach of the women’s game globally - driving the visibility needed to help inspire the next generation of players and fans.Across our partner clubsWe are incredibly proud to collaborate with Arsenal FC, FC Barcelona, FC Bayern München, Liverpool FC and Paris Saint-Germain - clubs that represent the very best of football heritage and community across Europe's top leagues. title: Bring your spreadsheet data to life with Sheets canvas
content:
Bring your spreadsheet data to life with Sheets canvas Aug 13, 2026 | A new Google Sheets feature, Sheets canvas transforms rows and columns into interactive dashboards, custom study trackers, seating charts, and more, all with a simple prompt. Eric Birnbaum Director, Product Management, Google Sheets

Google Sheets now features Sheets canvas, a tool that uses artificial intelligence to turn your data into interactive, visual mini-apps without any coding. You can simply describe your needs to Gemini, and it will build custom layouts like study trackers or seating charts that sync automatically with your original spreadsheet. To get started, open a sheet and click the Gemini icon to select "create canvas."

"Bring your spreadsheet data to life with Sheets canvas" turns boring data into interactive apps.

Use simple prompts to let Gemini build custom, visual layouts for your spreadsheets.

Your canvas and spreadsheet stay perfectly synced, so your data is always up to date.

You don't need coding skills to design dashboards, study trackers, or seating charts.

Share your canvas with others easily, just like you would with any regular sheet.

Google Sheets now has a new feature called Sheets canvas that turns boring rows of data into interactive, easy-to-read apps. You just tell AI what you want, and it builds a custom layout for you without any coding. Everything stays perfectly synced, so any changes you make update your original spreadsheet automatically. It’s a great way to organize school projects, sports stats, or event planning without getting overwhelmed.

Explore other styles:

General summary

Bullet points

Basic explainer

Spreadsheets are a powerful tool for organizing and understanding data, but staring at hundreds of rows and columns can sometimes feel a bit overwhelming. Whether you’re planning a wedding, tracking school assignments, managing a fantasy football roster, or comparing side hustle income, you want to see what you need to know from your data quickly.To help get you there, we’re introducing Sheets canvas, a new feature built with Gemini that turns your Google Sheets spreadsheets into custom, interactive "mini-apps." With a simple natural language prompt, you can transform your data into a visual experience that’s easy to understand and even easier to use.Visualize your data in new waysSheets canvas is a dynamic, read-write layer that sits directly on top of your spreadsheet data. This means that you can visually organize, edit, and navigate your data in whatever layout you imagine.Here is what makes it so powerful.No coding required: No formulas or programming required. Just describe what you want — like "create a visual study tracker" — and Gemini builds it for you.Always in sync: Whether you make changes to your canvas or to your sheet, updates are synced between the canvas and the original sheet in real time.Easy to adjust: You can continue to polish and refine your Sheets canvas by prompting Gemini to make edits to layout, design, functionality, and more.Fully collaborative: Since it lives as a tab in Google Sheets, your canvas can be shared with anyone, just like a regular sheet.See it in actionWe designed Sheets canvas to be as flexible as your imagination. Here are a few examples to show how you can start using it today.1. Stay on top of the school year For students, managing multiple subjects and deadlines is a full-time job. With Sheets canvas, you can turn a long list of assignments into an interactive study aid. Track progress, set reminders, and visualize the week ahead so you never miss a deadline.2. Dominate your fantasy football league Take your fantasy team to the next level by using Sheets canvas to build the ultimate command center for your roster. Create a custom dashboard to track player performance, compare stats side by side, and clearly visualize your path to the championship — all powered by the data in your sheet.3. Simplify wedding planning Juggling seating arrangements and meal choices just got infinitely easier. Sheets canvas transforms your guest RSVP data into an interactive seating chart. Just drag and drop guests to their tables, and rest easy knowing your central sheet stays up to date.Try it nowSheets canvas is now available globally in English to Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers. It's rolling out starting today to Google Workspace customers on Business or Enterprise Standard and Plus plans, and to Google AI Pro for Education add-on subscribers.Ready to see your data in a whole new light? Open a Google Sheets spreadsheet and select the “Create canvas” option in the Ask Gemini side panel to get started. Check out this article for more tips. Get the latest news from Google in your inbox Sign up for our newsletters with product updates, event information, special offers, and more. Done. Just one step more. Check your inbox to confirm your subscription. You can also subscribe with a different email address. Your information will be used in accordance with Google's privacy policy. You may opt out at any time. POSTED IN:
author: Eric Birnbaum

Google Sheets 现在推出了名为 Sheets Canvas 的新功能，它能将枯燥的数据行转化为交互式、易读的应用程序。你只需告诉 AI 你的需求，它便会为你构建自定义布局，全程无需编码。所有内容保持完美同步，你在 Canvas 中所做的任何更改都会自动更新到原始电子表格中。这是组织学校项目、体育统计数据或活动策划的绝佳方式，且不会让人感到不知所措。

电子表格是组织和理解数据的强大工具，但面对数百行和列时，有时可能会让人感到有些不知所措。无论你是在筹备婚礼、跟踪学校作业、管理梦幻橄榄球队阵容，还是比较副业收入，你都希望快速从数据中获取所需信息。为了帮助你实现这一目标，我们推出了 Sheets Canvas——一项基于 Gemini 构建的新功能，可将你的 Google Sheets 电子表格转化为定制的交互式“迷你应用”。只需使用简单的自然语言提示，即可将你的数据转变为易于理解且更易使用的可视化体验。以全新方式可视化你的数据
Sheets Canvas 是一个动态的读写层，直接叠加在电子表格数据之上。这意味着你可以按照自己设想的任何布局，对数据进行可视化组织、编辑和导航。这正是其强大之处所在。无需编写代码：不需要公式或编程知识。只需描述你的需求——例如“创建一个视觉化学习追踪器”——Gemini 就会为你生成。始终同步：无论你对 Canvas 还是对原始工作表进行修改，更新都会实时同步到 Canvas 和原始工作表之间。轻松调整：你可以通过向 Gemini 发出提示，继续完善和优化 Sheets Canvas 的布局、设计、功能等。完全支持协作：由于它作为 Google Sheets 中的一个标签页存在，因此可以像普通工作表一样与任何人共享。实战演示
我们设计 Sheets Canvas 的初衷是让它和你的想象力一样灵活。以下是一些示例，展示您今天即可开始使用它的方法。1. 紧跟学年节奏 对学生而言，同时管理多门课程和截止日期犹如一份全职工作。借助 Sheets Canvas，您可以将冗长的作业清单转化为互动式学习助手。跟踪进度、设置提醒并可视化未来一周的安排，确保您不错过任何截止日期。2. 称霸您的梦幻橄榄球联盟 利用 Sheets Canvas 为您的阵容打造终极指挥中心，将您的梦幻球队提升至新高度。创建自定义仪表板以追踪球员表现、并列对比统计数据，并清晰呈现您通往冠军之路——这一切均由您表格中的数据驱动。3. 简化婚礼筹备 协调座位安排和餐饮选择变得前所未有的轻松。Sheets Canvas 将您的宾客回复（RSVP）数据转化为互动式座位图。只需将宾客拖放到相应餐桌，即可安心放心，因为您的中心表格会始终保持最新状态。立即试用

title: AMIE, our research medical AI system, demonstrates real-time clinical video consultation capabilities in a first-of-its-kind study.
content:
AMIE, our research medical AI system, demonstrates real-time clinical video consultation capabilities in a first-of-its-kind study. Anil Palepu Research Lead Aug 11, 2026

When you visit a doctor, a consultation extends far beyond words — a physician notices a cough, observes gait, or registers visible signs of discomfort. Today, Google Research and Google DeepMind are advancing AMIE, our research medical AI system, toward real-time clinical video consultations, with a first-of-its-kind demonstration of expert-level AI capabilities in this setting. Built on Gemini and Project Astra using a multi-agent architecture, AMIE now interprets visual and auditory cues, guides virtual physical exams, and reasons diagnostically in real time.In a randomized study using simulated consultations with patient actors and a group of primary care physicians, clinical evaluators assessed AMIE favorably across core clinical competencies, including history-taking thoroughness, diagnostic accuracy, management appropriateness and communication quality. Patient actors also preferred the video experience over text chat.AMIE remains a research system and more research is needed before responsible real-world clinical deployment, but it offers an exciting glimpse into the future of health AI. Read more on the Google Research blog.

translated_paragraphs: AMIE，我们的研究医疗AI系统，在一项首创研究中展示了实时临床视频咨询能力。Anil Palepu 研究主管 2026年8月11日

当您去看医生时，问诊远不止于言语——医生会注意到咳嗽、观察步态，或察觉可见的不适迹象。如今，Google Research 和 Google DeepMind 正在推进 AMIE（我们的研究型医疗 AI 系统）向实时临床视频问诊发展，并在此场景中首次展示了专家级 AI 能力。AMIE 基于 Gemini 和 Project Astra，采用多智能体架构，现在能够解读视觉和听觉线索，引导虚拟体格检查，并实时进行诊断推理。在一项使用患者演员模拟问诊和一组初级保健医生的随机研究中，临床评估者对 AMIE 在核心临床能力方面给予了积极评价，包括病史采集的彻底性、诊通用准确性、管理适当性和沟通质量。患者演员也更喜欢视频体验而非文字聊天。AMIE仍然是一个研究系统，在负责任地部署到现实临床之前还需要更多研究，但它展示了健康AI未来的激动人心的一瞥。在Google Research博客上了解更多。

title: How canvases make agentic workflows visible, steerable, and cost-efficient
content:
When I was in college, I joined the beta for one of the first versions of AI inline completions in VS Code. It felt like a game changer. Since then, GenAI has fundamentally changed software development: hybrid teams where agents and humans work in tandem, with the developer at the center as visionary and orchestrator. We are living in that transition right now.

As a natural byproduct of how fast innovation in GenAI has moved, we now have tools to help us plan, build, review, and ship code. But in the current state, many workflows still feel disjointed. Context gets lost across threads and surfaces, and too much time gets spent reviewing agent-generated work. Agents can produce changes faster than any human can review them, and most developer tools were not originally designed for multi-agent orchestration. It becomes easy to lose track of what ran, what changed, what was validated, and what still needs human judgment.

The GitHub Copilot app is a major step toward addressing this. One feature in particular that I’ve learned to love and use almost every day is canvases. Canvases let developers and agents interact on a durable, shared surface. Instead of treating chat as the only place where work happens, canvases make work visible, steerable, and approvable as it unfolds.

Chat is great for intent, but weak for durable execution

I still believe chat is one of the best interfaces we have for intent. It’s where you can think, refine, and direct. It’s fast and flexible, especially when the problem is still ambiguous.

But once an agent starts doing real work, chat becomes a long scroll of instructions, logs, pivots, and corrections. The important parts are technically there, but buried: the plan, decision points, validations, and approval moments. If you have to reconstruct all of that from history, you’re already paying a coordination tax.

Canvases solve that by giving workflows a home. They make state explicit and persistent. Humans can inspect and guide. Agents can update and progress. Both can stay aligned without constantly replaying context.

The first build: Java Modernization Studio

One of the first canvases I built was Java Modernization Studio. Java modernization is exactly the kind of workflow where visibility and governance matter: assessment, planning, migration tasks, validation gates, and readiness to ship.

In a chat-only experience, those steps blur together. You can still move forward, but it gets harder to audit and harder to trust at scale, especially with multiple contributors. Teams keep asking the same expensive questions: What stage are we in? What decisions were made? What is blocked? What still needs human approval?

The studio made each phase explicit and inspectable. Instead of parsing narrative history, teams could see operational state directly. Instead of guessing what happened, they could verify it. Human reviewers could focus on high-signal judgments while agents kept execution moving between checkpoints.

Explore the Java Modernization Studio canvas >

The second build: Site Studio

After that, I built Site Studio for a very different workflow: creating and managing personal site content. It’s content-heavy rather than migration-heavy, but the orchestration challenge is similar: section progress, iterative edits, review loops, and status transitions.

In a chat-only flow, content can drift quickly. A section gets revised, then revised again, and confidence drops in what is current. Feedback gets scattered, drafts repeat, and momentum slows because each iteration starts by rebuilding context.

Site Studio keeps that state durable. Section status is visible. Draft values are persisted as work happens. Human review points are explicit. The agent can keep moving while the human can steer, approve, or redirect without losing the thread.

Explore the Site Studio canvas >

The repeatable pattern

Across both canvases, I found the same repeatable blueprint:

Define workflow states clearly.

Surface the decisions that matter.

Persist progress and drafts immediately.

Keep explicit human approval points.

This shifts the model from prompt-by-prompt interaction to durable collaborative workflows. You stop treating each turn like a fresh start and start treating each workflow like a system with memory, structure, and control.

Cost and efficiency: yes, canvases are an investment

I also want to be explicit about cost: canvases can be an investment. For instance, Site Studio cost me about 2,000 AI credits, and the modernization canvas cost me about 3,000 AI credits. They take effort to design and shape well.

But in the long run, especially for repeated workflows, that investment pays back. Durable surfaces reduce repeated prompting, reduce context loss, reduce unnecessary back-and-forth, and reduce rework. Over time, that can save both time and money while improving trust and throughput.

So for me, this is not “spend more tokens for nicer UX.” It’s “invest in better workflow architecture so recurring work becomes more efficient, predictable, and governable.”

Available now in awesome-copilot

The canvases I built—Java Modernization Studio and Site Studio—are available in awesome-copilot for anyone who wants to use them, adapt them, or learn from them.

If you are already using Copilot agents, a practical next step is to pick one repeated workflow and build a minimal canvas around it with /create-canvas. Start small, run real work, and iterate from actual usage. If it helps your team, contribute it back to awesome-copilot so others can benefit too.

We’re still early in this transition, but the direction is clear. Agents can accelerate execution. Humans provide vision, judgment, and accountability. Canvases are one way to make that partnership real, durable, and scalable.

translated_paragraphs: 大学期间，我参与了 VS Code 中最早一批 AI 行内补全功能的测试。那感觉堪称颠覆性变革。自此以来，生成式 AI 从根本上改变了软件开发：形成了智能体与人类协同工作的混合团队，开发者则居于核心，扮演愿景设定者与协调者的角色。我们正身处这一转型之中。
作为生成式 AI 创新速度飞快的自然产物，我们现在拥有了帮助规划、构建、审查和交付代码的工具。但在当前状态下，许多工作流仍然显得支离破碎。上下文在线程和不同界面之间容易丢失，而用于审查智能体生成内容的时间又过多。智能体产生变更的速度远超任何人工审查的能力，且大多数开发者工具最初并非为多智能体编排而设计。因此，很容易迷失方向，不清楚哪些已运行、哪些发生了变更、哪些已通过验证，以及哪些仍需人类判断。
GitHub Copilot 应用是解决这一问题的重要一步。其中有一个功能让我几乎每天都在使用并深深喜爱，那就是“画布”（Canvases）。画布让开发者和智能体能够在持久、共享的表面上进行交互。画布不再将聊天视为唯一的工作场所，而是使工作过程变得可见、可控且可审批。
聊天擅长表达意图，但在持久执行方面表现较弱
我依然认为，聊天是我们拥有的最佳意图接口之一。它是思考、细化和指导的地方。它快速而灵活，尤其在问题尚不明确时更是如此。
但一旦代理开始执行实际工作，聊天界面就会变成一份长长的指令、日志、转向和更正记录。关键信息虽然在技术层面存在，但却被埋没其中：计划、决策点、验证环节以及审批时刻。如果你必须从历史记录中重新梳理这些信息，就已经在支付协调成本了。
画布（Canvases）通过为工作流提供专属空间来解决这一问题。它使状态变得显式且持久化。人类可以检查和引导，代理可以更新并推进。双方无需不断重放上下文即可保持对齐。
首个构建：Java 现代化工作室
我构建的早期画布之一是 Java 现代化工作室。Java 现代化正是那种对可见性和治理至关重要的工作流类型：包括评估、规划、迁移任务、验证关卡以及发布准备就绪度。
在仅依赖聊天的体验中，这些步骤容易混为一谈。你仍然可以继续推进，但随着规模扩大，审计变得更加困难，信任也难以建立，尤其是在有多名贡献者参与的情况下。团队不断提出那些高昂的问题：我们处于哪个阶段？做出了哪些决策？什么被阻塞了？还有哪些需要人工审批？
该工作室使每个阶段都变得明确且可检查。团队不再需要解析叙述性的历史记录，而是可以直接查看操作状态；不再需要猜测发生了什么，而是能够进行验证。人工审核员可以专注于高价值判断，而代理则在各个检查点之间持续推动执行。

title: Frontier Model Cost and Open-Weights Popularity is Driving Demand for Model Routing
content:
Glean CEO Arvind Jain explains why model routing helps control AI costs for organizations, and how human feedback loops at scale improve its routing systems.

With the intense competition among frontier model companies, together with ever-increasing power of open-weight models like Kimi K3 and Qwen3.8-Max, model routing has become a key part of AI deployment. We’ve just seen Stripe buy OpenRouter for over $7B, but the trend is equally hot in enterprises.

Glean, co-founded and led by ex-Google Distinguished Engineer Arvind Jain, specializes in bringing AI to large organizations. It was last valued at $7.2B after a $150M Series F fund raise last June. This year, it reached $300 million in annual recurring revenue (ARR) — a three-fold increase over 15 months.

Part of Glean’s mission is to select which model to use for each task — or indeed if an LLM is even required.

“A big goal of Glean is to avoid using LLMs for tasks where we don’t need them,” Jain told Latent Space. “Sometimes you’ll see queries in Glean where people are adding two numbers or multiplying two numbers. They could have used a calculator to do that.”

But what Glean is mostly trying to do is bring what Jain calls “one really powerful personal co-worker” to enterprise employees. And that means being a kind of meta-harness for leading LLMs.

“You can think of Glean today as a superset of ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Grok,” Jain said. “All these different AI products that we’ve been using day to day, Glean combines the power of all of them into one experience.”

With enterprises, bringing AI technology into an organization is just half the challenge. The other half is bringing organizational knowledge into the AI systems.

“Ultimately our business is to deeply understand your data, knowledge, and information, but also how work happens inside your company,” Jain said.

How model routing is done in Glean

So what does model routing mean in practice? Basically, Glean offers three levels of model selection:

Employees can explicitly choose a model.

Administrators can restrict models or impose usage limits.

Glean’s automatic mode selects a model dynamically for each task.

It turns out automatic mode is mostly chosen by Glean’s customers for economic reasons.

“Why are people talking about model routing? Why are they excited about it? It’s mostly because of cost,” Jain told us.

Another co-founder of Glean, engineering lead Tony Gentilcore, recently claimed that Glean “is 4x more cost-effective” than Claude Code, “averaging $0.45 per task versus $1.84 for Claude Cowork.” He put that down to Glean’s “harness and routing capabilities.”

Individually, many of us are getting great value out of our $20, $100 or $200 monthly subscription to an LLM provider. But for an enterprise, the per-user costs can easily spiral out of control.

“AI models have been getting expensive,” Jain said. “Like, if you look at Opus or the latest models of GPT, the most advanced models. Not only are they very powerful, they can run much more complex tasks than the previous models. But on a per token basis, they’re more expensive — sometimes double or quadruple the rates of the previous models. And then users actually use them to run much longer tasks. So you’re spending, like, 10 times, 20 times, more, on a per user basis, than what you were doing last year. So the costs have gone up a lot.”

The human feedback loop

Another key factor in Glean’s rise is that it gets to see how ordinary business users are using AI. The product is potentially deployed to every employee as a “coworker,” and it’s also used to build and deploy agents across all departments and functions.

Among its customers, Zillow reports 80% adoption across 7,000 employees, while at Booking.com, “Glean became the first AI platform adopted company-wide.” That kind of penetration gives Glean an enviable view into how AI is being used in enterprises.

“So we are getting to observe what people are actually doing with AI on a very broad basis,” said Jain. “We are getting to see when they’re on different types of tasks with AI, what models do they select first, and when they are not satisfied, when they actually upgrade to some other model [that] actually gives them the right results.”

This human feedback loop, at scale, helps improve the model routing system.

Here’s Waldo, gathering raw materials

Another part of Glean’s architecture is a model called Waldo, which Jain described as sitting on top of the large language models. Waldo was introduced in April as “Glean’s first agentic search model.”

In a technical blog post, Waldo was portrayed as a kind of filtering process for user queries: it “decides how to break down the question, which tools to use, what to read next, and when it has enough evidence to hand off to a frontier model for a high-quality answer.”

This means the model routing is happening after Glean has determined what Jain calls the “raw materials” that are needed for the task.

“We’re able to assemble the raw materials needed to do the work without burning LLM tokens,” he added.

A corollary of this is that a cheaper model with better context may outperform a frontier model loaded with irrelevant data.

The rapid rise of open-weight models

Jain confirmed there is now significant interest from enterprises in open-weight models, primarily due to cost concerns. But this has only happened over the past few months.

“Last year, the usage [of open source LLMs] was minuscule and nobody was really seriously considering open source,” he said. Partly that was because of the “stigma” of many of these open source models being developed outside the US.

But suddenly, interest among enterprise customers has risen.

“So in the last three months, because AI got so expensive, businesses have started to find it untenable to maintain these AI investments,” Jain said. “Given that open source is an order of magnitude cheaper to do tasks, it has created a lot of interest. Today, I can say that in most enterprises, they are considering open source models to be a key part of their AI strategy.”

More than that, organizations tend not to rely on just one or two providers anymore — and the rise of open-weight models is driving this trend.

“Nobody is willing anymore to rely on only one model provider, or two, and nobody thinks that they can survive without open source,” Jain said.

Evals

You can’t have a serious conversation about AI in 2026 without discussing evals — assessing the quality of results from LLMs. I asked how Glean goes about doing evals and how that is fed back into the model routing system.

Jain said they have “internal testing systems” where they compare real-world workloads, across different query classes, with alternative options. So they let the model choose a route and in parallel they try to complete the same task with “some other models which are maybe a little bit less expensive and a little bit more expensive.”

Glean then uses “AI-based judges” to determine “how spot-on the model router was.”

“So there’s this continuous learning that gets updated with new real-world traffic, where basically what is happening is that you let the model router do the work for the user, but behind the scenes you run the same task,” Jain explained.

He added that this is done for only “a small fraction” of the real-world usage, but at Glean’s scale that’s more than enough to help train and improve the model router.

From enterprise search to end-to-end AI platform

One of the trends we’ll be monitoring going forward on Latent Space is how AI systems are being implemented within enterprises — and how some of these organizations are going full-on AI-native.

Glean is an especially interesting company to monitor for these trends, since it was one of the very first enterprise-facing AI companies. It was founded in early 2019, initially to tackle enterprise search. As Jain put it, Glean was “the first player to work with transformers and language models for businesses.”

In April 2023, swyx interviewed Deedy Das of Glean. Das, who is now a partner at venture firm Menlo Ventures, was a founding engineer at Glean. But even at that point, in 2023 — about four years into Glean — the focus was still mostly on enterprise search.

Now, in 2026, enterprises aren’t just using AI for search. AI is becoming an integral part of every employee’s workflow.

That makes Glean a much ‘sexier’ AI company, as Das himself said on his return to the Latent Space podcast last November. “Broadly, one of the things that I love about Glean is it’s such a boring unsexy company that became sexy later,” he said.

This brings us full circle back to model routing. Arvind Jain ended our discussion by calling Glean an “end-to-end AI platform” that gets “used very heavily” by its enterprise customers. This, he added, allows Glean to “have that data that is required to do effective model routing.”

One of the trends we’ll be monitoring going forward on Latent Space is how AI systems are being implemented within enterprises — and how some of these organizations are going full-on AI-native.

Now, in 2026, enterprises aren’t just using AI for search. AI is becoming an integral part of every employee’s workflow.

"AI模型的成本正在不断攀升，" Jain表示。"比如，如果你看看Opus或者GPT的最新模型，也就是那些最先进的模型，它们不仅能力非常强大，能够执行比之前模型复杂得多的任务，而且按每个token计算，它们的费用更高——有时是之前模型费率的两倍甚至四倍。此外，用户实际上会用它们来运行更长的任务。因此，从单个用户的角度来看，你花费的金额可能是去年的10倍、20倍。所以成本大幅上升了。"
人类反馈循环
Glean崛起的关键因素之一在于，它能够观察到普通业务用户如何使用AI。该产品有望作为“同事”部署给每一位员工，同时也用于在各个部门和职能中构建和部署智能体（agents）。
在其客户中，Zillow报告称7,000名员工中的采用率高达80%，而在Booking.com，“Glean成为首家在公司范围内采用的AI平台”。这种渗透率使Glean得以令人羡慕地洞察企业在AI使用方面的实际情况。
"因此，我们能够非常广泛地观察人们实际如何使用AI，" Jain说。"我们能看到他们在不同类型的任务中使用AI的情况，他们首先选择哪些模型，以及当他们不满意时，何时会升级到其他能真正提供正确结果的模型。"
这种大规模的人类反馈循环有助于改进模型路由系统。
这是Waldo，正在收集原材料
Glean架构的另一部分是一个名为Waldo的模型，Jain将其描述为“坐”在大型语言模型之上的组件。Walo于四月作为“Glean的首个智能体搜索模型”推出。
在一篇技术博客文章中，Waldo被描绘成一种对用户查询进行过滤处理的机制：它“决定如何拆解问题、使用哪些工具、下一步阅读什么内容，以及在拥有足够证据时何时将任务移交至前沿模型以生成高质量答案。”
这意味着，在Glean确定了Jain所称的任务所需“原材料”之后，才会发生模型路由过程。
他补充道：“我们能够在不消耗大型语言模型令牌（tokens）的情况下，组装完成工作所需的原材料。”
由此得出的一个推论是，一个成本更低但上下文更精准的模型，可能会胜过那些充斥着无关数据的前沿模型。
开源权重模型的迅速崛起
Jain证实，企业界对开源权重模型的兴趣如今显著增加，主要原因在于成本考量。不过，这一趋势仅在过去几个月内出现。
他说：“去年，[开源大型语言模型]的使用量微乎其微，没有人真正认真考虑过开源方案。”部分原因在于，许多此类开源模型由美国以外的机构开发，因而背负着某种“污名”。
但突然间，企业客户中的兴趣开始上升。
“因此，在过去三个月里，由于人工智能成本大幅上升，企业开始认为维持这些AI投资变得难以承受。”Jain表示。“鉴于开源模型在执行任务时的成本低出一个数量级，它引发了大量关注。如今，我可以断言，在大多数企业中，它们已将开源模型视为其AI战略的关键组成部分。”
不仅如此，组织也不再仅仅依赖一两家供应商——而开放权重模型的兴起正推动这一趋势。
“如今，没有人愿意只依赖单一或两家模型提供商，也没有人认为离开开源还能生存下去。”Jain说。
评估（Evals）
如果在2026年要严肃讨论人工智能，就不可避免地要谈到评估（evals）——即对大语言模型输出结果的质量进行评估。我询问了Glean如何进行评估，以及评估结果如何反馈到模型路由系统中。

随后，Glean会使用“基于AI的裁判”来判断“模型路由器的决策是否精准到位”。
“因此，这是一个持续学习的过程，会随着新的真实流量不断更新。基本上，你让用户侧由模型路由器代为处理请求，但在后台，系统会并行执行相同的任务。”Jain解释道。
他补充说，这一做法仅针对实际使用中的“一小部分”，但在Glean的规模下，这已经足以帮助训练和改进模型路由器。

title: Origin Code Hosting
content:
Aug 17, 2026 · Changelog

Cursor can now host your code.

Origin begins rolling out today in early beta on all paid plans. We're starting with the essentials, designed for agent scale: repos, pull requests, code browsing, and GitHub sync. Agent-native features ship soon.

#Origin Repos

The new Codebase tab is home for Origin repos.

Click +New to create a new repo and name it. Once you do, a page shows you how to install the CLI, with commands for how to clone a repo or push a local project. Push, and your code is hosted on Origin.

Name your codebase when you create your first repo. That name becomes part of every repo's URL: cursor.com/codebase/acme-corp.

#Bring your GitHub repos

Your GitHub repos can sit alongside the ones Cursor hosts. Connect GitHub to Cursor, pick your org, and you'll see the repos you can sync. Select one and Cursor pulls it in. You choose what gets synced and can disconnect a repo at any time. Anyone with read or write access to a synced repo can view it in Cursor too.

Synced repos update in real time. Browse, search, and pull from the copy in Origin. Pushes keep going to GitHub, which stays the source of truth for anything started there. Icons next to each repo name tell you which ones Cursor hosts and which came from GitHub.

#Pull requests

Every repo has pull requests. Open one to see the timeline, commits, checks, and files changed. Review the diff, leave comments, and merge.

Pull requests on synced repos sync both ways: comment in Cursor and it posts to GitHub, react or reply on GitHub and it shows up in Cursor within seconds. Got a review assigned to you on GitHub? Review and merge it from Cursor.

#Agents in every repo

Your code, PRs, and agents are now in the same place. Ask Cursor questions about code you're browsing. It can answer, make changes, update PRs, or push a branch.

#App extensions for Cursor repos

We're building an app ecosystem so your whole stack works seamlessly with Origin. Integrations with Vercel, Depot, and Buildkite are already available, with more coming soon.

Connect Vercel from a repo's Apps tab and every PR gets a preview deployment where you can test and make comments. Merge, and it ships to production. For CI, connect Depot or Buildkite. Both run your existing GitHub Actions workflows and Buildkite also runs its native pipelines.

#Settings

Every repo has settings. Check sync status for GitHub repos, manage who has access, and see which apps are connected.

Origin is rolling out in early beta to all paid plan users starting today, except enterprise orgs whose admins opt out. Name your codebase and create your first repo.

Learn more in our docs or get started today.

translated_paragraphs: 2026年8月17日 · 更新日志
Cursor 现在可以托管你的代码。
Origin 将于今天开始在所有付费计划中推出早期测试版。我们首先推出的是专为智能体规模设计的基础功能：仓库、拉取请求、代码浏览和 GitHub 同步。原生支持智能体的功能即将上线。
# Origin 仓库
新的“代码库”标签页是 Origin 仓库的归属地。
点击“+新建”以创建新仓库并为其命名。完成后，页面会展示如何安装 CLI，并提供克隆仓库或推送本地项目的命令。执行推送后，你的代码即被托管在 Origin 上。
在创建第一个仓库时为代码库命名。该名称将成为每个仓库 URL 的一部分：cursor.com/codebase/acme-corp。
# 引入你的 GitHub 仓库
你的 GitHub 仓库可以与 Cursor 托管的仓库并列存放。将 GitHub 连接到 Cursor，选择组织，即可看到可同步的仓库。选择一个仓库，Cursor 便会将其拉入。你可以选择同步哪些内容，并且随时可以断开某个仓库的连接。任何对已同步仓库拥有只读或写入权限的人，也可以在 Cursor 中查看它。
已同步的仓库会实时更新。你可以在 Origin 中的副本上进行浏览、搜索和拉取操作。推送操作仍会发送至 GitHub，GitHub 保持为一切在该处启动的内容的唯一事实来源。每个仓库名称旁边的图标会指示该仓库是由 Cursor 托管还是来自 GitHub。
# 拉取请求
每个仓库都支持拉取请求。打开一个拉取请求即可查看时间线、提交记录、检查状态和变更文件。审查差异、留下评论并进行合并。
同步仓库的拉取请求支持双向同步：在 Cursor 中评论，便会发布到 GitHub；在 GitHub 上反应或回复，几秒钟内就会显示在 Cursor 中。如果在 GitHub 上分配了代码审查任务？可以直接从 Cursor 进行审查和合并。
#每个仓库中的智能体
你的代码、拉取请求和智能体现在都集中在同一位置。可以向 Cursor 询问你正在浏览的代码问题。它能够回答、进行修改、更新拉取请求或推送分支。
#Cursor 仓库的应用扩展
我们正在构建应用生态系统，使你的整个技术栈与 Origin 无缝协作。目前已有 Vercel、Depot 和 Buildkite 的集成，更多集成即将推出。
从仓库的“应用”选项卡连接 Vercel，每个拉取请求都会获得一个预览部署，你可以在其中测试并发表评论。合并后，即可部署到生产环境。对于持续集成（CI），可以连接 Depot 或 Buildkite。两者都能运行你现有的 GitHub Actions 工作流，而 Buildkite 还能运行其原生流水线。
#设置
每个仓库都有设置功能。可以查看 GitHub 仓库的同步状态、管理访问权限，以及查看已连接的应用程序。
Origin 今天开始向所有付费计划用户逐步开放早期测试版，企业组织的管理员可选择退出。为你的代码库命名并创建第一个仓库。
在我们的文档中了解更多，或立即开始使用。

title: Cloud Agents Start 3x Faster with Builds
content:
Aug 13, 2026 · Changelog

Agents do their best work when they start in a ready environment: repos cloned, dependencies installed, and your install script already run.

This release introduces builds: ready-to-use copies of your development environment that Cursor prepares in the background. Agents boot into a ready environment instead of setting up from scratch each session. Builds are included with Cloud Agents at no additional cost.

#Faster starts

Cursor runs a new build of your environment regularly. When a build succeeds, it becomes the environment future agents start from. Cursor keeps warm copies ready so the next agent does not wait. Internally, our environments now boot 10x faster, with 3x faster time to first token.

Use your install command for anything that can be prepared ahead of time. The start command still runs when you first prompt an agent and should focus on services that need to be fresh in the session.

#More resilient agent runs

When a bad commit or dependency update breaks your environment, agents keep using the last successful build. The broken build never becomes active, you are notified of the issue, and your agents keep working while you debug in the background.

#Build history and debugging

Each environment has a Builds tab in the Cloud Agents dashboard. You can inspect build status, logs, commit SHAs, and which build each agent run used. Agents can also inspect and manage builds using built-in tools.

#Getting started

New environments use Builds automatically. For an existing environment, open it in the Cloud Agents dashboard, go to the Builds tab, and click Enable Builds. Or click Run setup agent first to test the migration and review any proposed config changes.

You can also trigger a Build manually, debug a failing Build with an agent, and control how stale Builds refresh with a configurable threshold.

Learn more in our announcement post and docs.

translated_paragraphs: 2026年8月13日 · 更新日志
当代理程序在就绪的环境中启动时，它们能发挥最佳性能：代码仓库已克隆、依赖项已安装，并且您的安装脚本也已运行完毕。
本次发布引入了“构建”（Builds）功能：这是 Cursor 在后台准备的、开箱即用的开发环境副本。代理程序将直接启动到就绪环境中，而无需在每个会话中从头开始设置。构建功能随 Cloud Agents 免费提供，无需额外费用。
#启动更快
Cursor 会定期为您的环境创建新的构建。当某次构建成功时，它将成为未来代理程序的启动环境。Cursor 会保持预热副本就绪，以便下一个代理程序无需等待。内部数据显示，我们的环境启动速度提升了 10 倍，首个 Token 的生成时间缩短了 3 倍。
使用您的安装命令来准备任何可以预先完成的任务。启动命令仍会在您首次向代理程序发出提示时运行，应专注于那些需要在会话中保持最新状态的服务。
#更稳健的代理程序运行
当错误的提交或依赖项更新破坏了您的环境时，代理程序会继续使用上一次成功的构建。损坏的构建不会被激活，您会收到问题通知，同时代理程序在您后台调试的过程中继续正常工作。
#构建历史与调试
在 Cloud Agents 仪表板中，每个环境都有一个“构建”标签页。您可以检查构建状态、日志、提交 SHA 值以及每次代理程序运行所使用的构建版本。代理程序还可以使用内置工具检查和管理工作流。
#入门指南
新环境会自动使用构建功能。对于现有环境，请在 Cloud Agents 控制台中打开该环境，进入“构建”选项卡，然后点击“启用构建”。或者，您可以先点击“运行设置代理”以测试迁移并查看任何建议的配置更改。
您还可以手动触发构建、使用代理调试失败的构建，并通过可配置的阈值来控制过期构建的刷新方式。
更多信息请参阅我们的公告文章和文档。

title: Google Workspace Plugins
content:
Aug 3, 2026 · Changelog

Cursor can now read, write, and act across Google Workspace via plugins, so you can pull context, draft and update files, and manage your inbox and calendar without leaving Cursor.

Install plugins to connect:

Google Drive: search files and folders, open and download content, create and organize files
